 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Flagg being listed as questionable on the Mavericks’ initial injury report is good news for fantasy managers. After he sustained a shoulder injury during Friday’s win over the Pacers, expectations were that the reigning Rookie of the Year would miss a few days. Now, Flagg could miss just one game after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. If he returns, Zaccharie Risacher will head to the bench. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher recorded 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 After Cooper Flagg sustained a left shoulder injury in Friday’s win over the Pacers, Risacher started for the Mavericks for the first time on Saturday. He had a highlight-worthy block on Victor Wembanyama at the rim in the first half, but his overall production wasn’t enough to put Risacher on the streaming radar. Naji Marshall and PJ Washington (12 points, four rebounds and two assists) are better fantasy options until Flagg returns. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 Naji Marshall, Max Christie, Zaccharie Risacher, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 The Mavericks won’t have Cooper Flagg or Kyrie Irving on Saturday, with the former facing an extended absence after injuring his shoulder during Friday’s win over the Pacers. As a result, Marshall and Risacher will start, with Naji offering a higher ceiling for fantasy managers seeking a streamer. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is now probable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Dealing with a sore right hip, Risacher was initially questionable for Saturday’s game. With Cooper Flagg (shoulder) out and Kyrie Irving (knee) downgraded to doubtful, Risacher may have more offensive opportunities. However, Naji Marshall is a better option for managers seeking a streamer.

 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Risacher had 11 points off the bench in Friday’s win over the Pacers. With the Mavericks’ lengthy injury report, he could play at least 30 minutes again, though he’s probably not worth streaming in most fantasy leagues. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher scored 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a steal, three blocks, and a three in 32 minutes against the Pacers. 
 He started the first half with 11 points and ended the game with 11 points. Risacher took advantage of all the easy opportunities in front of him. He got out in transition and took efficient shots. It seems like the Mavs are really prioritizing him and will get ample opportunities this season, even if it’s not a starter. Dusty May likes to play players with length, skill, and athleticism and Risacher can fit that. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) has been ruled out against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Martin will start the season on the injury report. However, Dallas has more than enough depth in the frontcourt to make up for his absence. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher may take on a few extra minutes. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Zaccharie Risacher has been traded to the Mavericks in a deal that sends Luguentz Dort and Ryan Nembhard to the Hawks and three second-round picks to the Thunder. 
 The former No. 1 overall pick wasn’t able to figure things out in Atlanta, but he’ll get a fresh start in Dallas. With Masai Ujiri and Mike Schmitz running the show for the Mavs, they have rebuilt this roster around Cooper Flagg by adding multiple new players in the frontcourt, including Risacher, Santi Aldama and Morez Johnson. Risacher’s role will likely be limited off the bench to start his tenure with Dallas, though a fresh start on a rebuilding team could yield him the opportunity to develop into the player the Hawks hoped he would become. The three second-round picks heading to OKC are Chicago’s 2027 pick from Dallas and most favorable picks in 2031 and 2032 from Atlanta. 
 Onyeka Okongwu 
 ATL 
 Forward-Center 
 #17 
 Onyeka Okongwu (finger) and Jonathan Kuminga (knee) are questionable for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Okongwu and Kuminga sitting out Sunday’s regular-season finale would free up rotation minutes for multiple players. That includes Zaccharie Risacher, whose playing time has decreased with Kuminga in the fold, Asa Newell and Mouhamed Gueye. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Cavaliers. 
 After playing seven minutes in Monday’s loss to the Knicks, the first overall pick in the 2024 draft did not play at all on Wednesday. Jonathan Kuminga has seemingly absorbed the minutes that once went to Risacher. Logging 30 minutes, Kuminga finished with 24 points (11-of-20 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers. An afterthought in fantasy basketball since the All-Star break, it’s fair to wonder about Risacher’s future in Atlanta, especially if he racks up more DNP-CDs during the postseason.

 CJ McCollum lit up the Rockets with 20 points (8-of-16 FGs), one rebound, three assists, three steals and four three-pointers on Monday.
 McCollum has been a solid source of offense for the Hawks since they traded for him last season. So far this year, his production has been underwhelming, but this ended up being his best scoring performance of the season. He has been efficient as a scorer, but the lack of volume has prevented him from making much of an impact for fantasy managers. Still, as a starter, he’ll continue to produce standard-league value.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Jalen Johnson led the Hawks with 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in a 120-110 loss to the Rockets on Monday.
 It wasn’t as dominant of a performance as he put together against Houston on Saturday, but Johnson was still able to provide value across the board in the rematch. However, that didn’t change the result on the scoreboard. Johnson will continue to stuff the stat sheet for Atlanta, which has allowed him to be one of the best players in fantasy basketball so far this season despite a rough start shooting the ball.

 Jalen Green recorded 20 points (8-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Thunder.
 Green led four Suns starters with 20 points, two fewer than his total in Phoenix’s first two games. Efficiency has never been his strength, and that has limited Green’s value in category leagues.  Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Thunder with 19 points (4-of-14 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers.
 Brooks didn’t have a good night shooting the basketball, making three of his ten three-point attempts and going 4-of-14 overall. The good news is that he recorded a complete stat line, which is welcome for a player whose fantasy value has underwhelmed so far. Brooks’ 2025-26 output factored into his preseason ADP, as he exceeded many fantasy managers’ expectations last season.

 Isaiah Hartenstein accounted for 15 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 13 rebounds and three assists in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 With Chet Holmgren (knee) sitting out Monday’s game, Hartenstein was the lone 7-footer in the Thunder starting lineup. He recorded his second double-double in as many nights, and iHart’s ability to play both games of Oklahoma City’s back-to-back is encouraging. He appeared in 47 games last season, and injuries also contributed to Hartenstein’s minutes dropping by more than three per game. He’s looked healthy so far, which is critical with the Thunder losing Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) for the season on Sunday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Monday’s win over the Suns with 26 points (11-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one three-pointer.
 In the aftermath of the injuries to Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams, some may have expected Gilgeous-Alexander to shoot until his arm fell off. That didn’t happen, as the reigning MVP got his points while also trusting his teammates. SGA recorded just three assists, but he shot the ball well and extended his 20-point streak to 143 games. Oklahoma City plays two more games in Week 2, starting with the Mavericks on Wednesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jared McCain tallied 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 McCain was one of three replacements in the Thunder starting lineup on Monday. With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) needing surgery, McCain has a good chance of staying a starter for the long haul. He shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc against the Suns and recorded a complete stat line, playing 30 minutes. Like Ajay Mitchell, McCain is a must-add if he’s on the waiver wire. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ajay Mitchell

 Ajay Mitchell went off for 30 points (10-of-16 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) out for the foreseeable future, the Thunder will need greater contributions from players like Mitchell to stay afloat in the West. The third-year guard started on Monday and delivered the best game of his NBA career to date. Mitchell finished with his first 30-point game and was a steal shy of a complete stat line. If Mitchell is still on your league’s waiver wire, add him immediately.
